findings.description: This is the same AC9 class as r0-1, with a distinct cause the r1 fix did not reach. The skills registry's symlink secondary targets (.github/skills, .cursor/skills, ...) are replaced non-atomically with existsSync -> unlink -> symlink. When two runs overlap there, one gets ENOENT (unlink after the other's unlink) or EEXIST (symlink after the other's symlink). The registry is then reported failed and the install exits 1. Probe: two node processes each call distributeToSecondaryTargets 300 times on one real project (canonical .claude/skills plus a .github/skills symlink). Result: pid A ok 150 / EEXIST 119 / ENOENT 31; pid B ok 155 / EEXIST 107 / ENOENT 38. In-process Promise.all of two calls gives EEXIST 30/30. The race needs both runs' skills post-copy to overlap: 0/50 real concurrent full-dataset installs hit it, and concurrent-install.sh cannot reach it because its mock KB ships no skills registry.
findings.recommendation: Make the link replacement race-tolerant and last-writer-wins: create the link at a unique temp name and rename it over linkPath (atomic on POSIX), or treat ENOENT on unlink and EEXIST on symlink as a lost race and retry once. VERIFY: a unit test that runs two distributeToSecondaryTargets concurrently on a real temp dir (Promise.all, x30); ORACLE: AC9 'is not blocked and does not abort'; ASSERT: every call resolves and .github/skills is a symlink resolving to .claude/skills.
